A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LayoutVLM. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark, ablation, and VLM fine-tuning results in Tables 2–4, plus qualitative results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds human evaluation, agreement measurements, and further component ablations in Tables 3–5.

M1.justification: The numerical-pose/spatial-relation representation, visual prompting, grouping, self-consistent decoding, optimization objectives, and fine-tuning approach remain unchanged. V2 newly documents implementation details without establishing a revision to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 11 room types with Objaverse assets, approximately 9,000 3D-Front training rooms, and residential fine-tuning evaluations. Human ratings and additional ablations assess the retained layout task without extending its dataset or domain coverage.

E2.justification: LayoutGPT, Holodeck, and I-Design remain the benchmark comparators and also appear in the new human evaluation. The GPT-4o and LLaVA fine-tuning comparisons are retained. The additional variants are component ablations.

E3.justification: New Section 5.3 introduces a human-evaluation protocol: five graduate students rank methods for position, orientation, and overall performance, with 495 ratings reported per method/metric pair. GPT-4o scores are converted to rankings for comparison. Additional ablations introduce new controls, while existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands the component analysis with separate removals of asset marks, coordinates, all visual marks, and numerical initialization in Table 5. It adds a qualitative self-consistency comparison in Figure 6 and human validation of the automated evaluator. The repeated 'w/o (Spatial) Const.' row reproduces the existing 'w/o Const.' result.

E5.justification: V2 adds Kendall's tau estimates of user-user and user-GPT-4o agreement in Table 4. Existing mean-plus/minus reporting is retained; the additional ablation rows do not establish new uncertainty practices or increased run counts.

E6.justification: New results include human overall ranks of 1.50 for LayoutVLM and 2.64 for I-Design, plus human-GPT agreement estimates. Added ablations report PSA values of 52.2, 46.0, 43.0, and 41.0 for removing asset marks, coordinates, all marks, and numerical initialization, respectively. Earlier benchmark, ablation, and fine-tuning values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem assumptions and mathematical objectives, including Equations 1–7 and Appendix A.2, are retained. Changes to spatial-relation names and equation typography are not mathematical revisions; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The central claims about physically plausible, instruction-aligned layout generation, complementary representations, self-consistent decoding, and fine-tuning benefits remain the same. The abstract's revised spatial-reasoning motivation does not materially change their scope.

C2.justification: V2 interprets its human study as supporting agreement with GPT-4o evaluation. It also explicitly attributes physical validity to spatial constraints and better semantic scores to numerical initialization. The limitation concerning failures from suboptimal VLM initialization remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly specifies Adam, exponential learning-rate decay of 0.96, 400 optimization steps, projection every 100 steps, and runtime/GPU/API-call estimates. Section 5.5 adds room-type-based instruction generation, LoRA for LLaVA, and GPT-4o API fine-tuning. These are disclosures about existing experiments, not demonstrated setting changes.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 36 referenced works and the same positioning relative to LLM-based layout generation, search-based optimization, and VLM spatial reasoning. Added passages reuse existing references; bibliographic spelling and citation-location changes are editorial.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract opening, corrects an author name, adds a human-evaluation subsection, and extends the ablation, fine-tuning, and optimization descriptions. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 3–4 and Figure 6, expands the ablation table into grouped comparisons, and repositions retained figures and tables. Appendix Figure 6 becomes Figure 7 with the same examples. These are localized additions and layout adjustments within the retained visual format.

improvement.justification: V1 relies on GPT-4o evaluation supported by prior work; v2 adds direct human-agreement evidence, more informative component ablations, and useful implementation details. These strengthen empirical credibility and reproducibility. The five-rater study provides limited validation, and the core method and benchmark findings remain unchanged, making the overall gain incremental.
